analysis: Both units are head-side text of docs/provider/cli-reference.md, lines 1590-2484. The file's changed head ranges end at line 1527, and the complete range map shows none of these lines were modified, so the units are unchanged surrounding context. They cover the stop, uninstall, restart, status, doctor, verify, models, benchmark, update, beta, fan, login and logout command docs. I found no new security behavior, no contradiction of the TB-007, TB-011, T-041 or T-053 posture, and no invalidated assumption in this text. The text I read matches the documented model: uninstall refuses sudo, link targets and mount points; logout and uninstall revoke the token on a best-effort basis and say so; prefix-cache status stays consistent with T-041; and the App Attest traffic and lease wording stays consistent with the authorization contract. The substantive change in this PR is the new `darkbloom sandbox setup --disk <volume>` option and its Setup validation (patch hunks near head lines 1256-1324, outside these units). It touches TB-013 and T-061: work disks are passed to the add-on installer, and path and volume checks take external input. I did not see that text in these units. Another pass should check whether the documented path normalization, /Volumes validation and the statfs check make sense as a trust boundary. It should also check that the docs do not overclaim safety for operator-selected external volumes; T-041 notes that peripherals are outside the attested boundary. This is a docs-only change with no code evidence here.
